title: More US Households Now Have Kittens than Puppies
paragraphs: Dogs and cats are the most popular pets in the US. But there has been an interesting change. For the first time, more American households now have kittens than puppies.

This information comes from Packaged Facts, a company that does research on markets, including the pet market. The company has been tracking the number of households with puppies and kittens for many years. In 2025, the numbers became equal. Then, in 2026, kittens moved ahead. According to reports, there are now 0.94 households with puppies for every household with a kitten.

However, this does not mean that cats are suddenly much more popular. According to Packaged Facts, the change is mainly happening because fewer households own dogs. Between 2019 and 2025, the number of households with dogs fell by more than 4%. Meanwhile, the number of households with cats rose by 4%.
Kittens are young cats, and puppies are young dogs. These young animals are only a small part of the pet population. In 2025, only 7% of dog owners had puppies, while 11% of cat owners had kittens.

There may be several reasons for this change. According to some reports, owning a dog is becoming more expensive. Dogs can also need more time and space than cats, as they need to be walked every day.

Even so, dogs remain very popular in the US. Many Americans still say they prefer dogs to cats. However, some experts say that the pet industry, which has often focused more on dogs, may now need to pay more attention to the needs of cats and their owners.
